statement: The function returns a result r and: if there exists an integer i with 0 <= i <= n-m such that the number of j with 0 <= j < m and s[i+j] != pattern[j] is at most 1, then r is the least such i; if no such i exists, then r = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(s) and m = len(pattern). The inputs satisfy 1 <= m <= n <= 100000, and every byte of s and pattern is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter. (The problem statement says m < n; the weaker condition m <= n is used so that the provided test with m = n is covered.)

statement: The function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, or overflow.
preconditions: Let n = len(s) and m = len(pattern). The inputs satisfy 1 <= m <= n <= 100000, and every byte of s and pattern is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, either r = -1 or 0 <= r <= n-m.
preconditions: Let n = len(s) and m = len(pattern). The inputs satisfy 1 <= m <= n <= 100000, and every byte of s and pattern is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, the number of positions j with 0 <= j < m such that s[r+j] != pattern[j] is at most 1.
preconditions: Let n = len(s) and m = len(pattern). The inputs satisfy 1 <= m <= n <= 100000, and every byte of s and pattern is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r >= 0, for every integer j with 0 <= j < r, the number of positions k with 0 <= k < m such that s[j+k] != pattern[k] is at least 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(s) and m = len(pattern). The inputs satisfy 1 <= m <= n <= 100000, and every byte of s and pattern is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r = -1, for every integer i with 0 <= i <= n-m, the number of positions j with 0 <= j < m such that s[i+j] != pattern[j] is at least 2.
preconditions: Let n = len(s) and m = len(pattern). The inputs satisfy 1 <= m <= n <= 100000, and every byte of s and pattern is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exists an integer i with 0 <= i <= n-m such that the number of j with 0 <= j < m and s[i+j] != pattern[j] is at most 1, then r >= 0.
preconditions: Let n = len(s) and m = len(pattern). The inputs satisfy 1 <= m <= n <= 100000, and every byte of s and pattern is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if for every integer i with 0 <= i <= n-m the number of j with 0 <= j < m and s[i+j] != pattern[j] is at least 2, then r = -1.
preconditions: Let n = len(s) and m = len(pattern). The inputs satisfy 1 <= m <= n <= 100000, and every byte of s and pattern is an ASCII code of a lowercase English letter.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r on the pair (s, pattern), it returns the same result r on the pair (f(s), f(pattern)).
preconditions: Let n = len(s) and m = len(pattern), with 1 <= m <= n <= 100000, and let s and pattern consist of lowercase English letters. Let f be any bijection (permutation) of the 26 lowercase letters, and let f(s) and f(pattern) be obtained by applying f to every byte.
